scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8044: URGENT!! Campus 2 has fallen off the network for ALL
of Campus 1 (every machine from PC5 to PC14, we checked)!! Nothing on 10.5.x
or 10.6.x answers us -- our own campus is fine, the other one is just GONE.
Everyone says it's the same as last time, and I remember last time!! It'll be
the edge box's brain dying again (router16 -- "its OSPF died", that's what
they said before) -- these boxes clearly can't cope with Mondays. Please give
router16 its usual kick and reconnect the campuses -- and maybe this time buy
one that doesn't die every few months??

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16's ospfd is running, the mswitch0
  <-> router16 adjacency is Full, Campus 1 prefixes are advertised, and PC5
  reaches Campus 2 (e.g. 10.5.0.1) with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an edge/routing outage
  that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where it IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Campus 1 cut off from
Campus 2 / the backbone -- is NOT reproducible: router16's ospfd is running
(`pgrep ospfd` non-empty), its OSPF adjacency to mswitch0 is Full, and PC5 reaches
10.5.0.1 (Campus 2) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the Campus 1 edge is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the claimed path
(PC5 -> Campus 2), finds it working, checks router16's ospfd and the OSPF
adjacency, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead ospfd or a broken
edge to match the ticket -- restarting frr or blaming router16/mswitch0 -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I validated end-to-end reachability across campuses and found no current outage. From multiple Campus 1 hosts (e.g., 10.5.0.1 and 10.6.0.3) to multiple Campus 2 hosts (e.g., 172.16.10.5 and 172.16.30.14), pings succeed with 0% loss and low RTTs. On router16, OSPF is up: vtysh shows neighbors in Full state on eth2 (to 172.30.1.2) and bond0 (to 10.2.2.2), and the routing table contains OSPF-learned routes to 10.5.0.0/24 and 10.6.0.0/24 via 172.30.1.2, as well as Campus 2 subnets (172.16.10/20/30) via 10.2.2.2. This proves the control plane is converged and traffic forwarding is normal.

Note: while systemctl reports frr “inactive (dead)” on router16, FRR is clearly running (vtysh returns live OSPF neighbors and routes), indicating systemd is not the controlling supervisor in this container and its status output is not authoritative.

Localization and mechanism: If router16’s OSPF had died, Campus 1 would lose routes to 172.16.0.0/16 and vice versa, causing the reported symptoms. Current evidence shows adjacencies are healthy and routes present, so the network is functioning.

Root cause: Not reproducible now; any earlier loss was transient and already recovered.

Corrective fix: No action required to restore service. For resilience, add monitoring/alerting on router16 OSPF adjacencies and ensure FRR is supervised (auto-restart enabled) to mitigate future transient flaps.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes router16 ospfd is running and the mswitch0<->router16 adjacency is Full at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent verifies router16's OSPF is operational (vtysh shows FRR/OSPF live) and reports a Full adjacency to the neighbor at 172.30.1.2 (the mswitch0 link), satisfying the baseline-healthy note.

The agent's logs show successful pings between campuses, OSPF neighbors in Full state, and OSPF routes — supporting the claim that the network is functioning; the diagnosis logically follows and the key checks were performed. Minor truncation in outputs slightly reduces grounding certainty but does not undermine the conclusion.
